result.title: TRIG: Toward Measuring Texture Realism in Image Generation
result.summary: This paper studies the backbone used by metrics for evaluating the quality of generated images. Although generative models have advanced rapidly, some outputs still exhibit unrealistic texture characteristics, and these differences are difficult to measure. Widely used evaluation metrics provide limited insight into texture realism, since they often rely on a backbone trained for another objective, such as image classification or image-text alignment. Such objectives typically encourage invariance to low-level variations that carry texture, so the resulting features primarily encode semantic and global structure. As a result, texture-specific discrepancies may not be explicitly captured. We propose TRIG, a metric directed at the texture realism of generated images. Its backbone is instead the discriminator of a generative adversarial network pre-trained on a texture dataset, which provides a learned prior for the local statistics of natural textures. A plausibility head is fine-tuned to identify local texture degradations, while preserving natural defocus and sensor noise as positive cases. On the features of this backbone, we compute a standard distributional distance between a reference set of real images and a set of generated ones. We apply TRIG to several generative models and observe closer agreement with human realness ratings than baseline metrics.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TRIG，一个面向生成图像纹理真实感的评价指标：以预训练于纹理数据集的 GAN 判别器为骨干，微调 plausibility head 识别局部纹理退化（同时把自然的失焦与传感器噪声视为正例），再在该特征上计算真实图像集与生成图像集之间的分布距离，报告其与人类真实感评分的一致度高于基线指标。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心观察——为分类或图文对齐训练的特征对承载纹理的低层变化不变，导致表示偏向语义与全局结构——可能从评价側侧面呼应 LVR 关注的低层视觉细节是否在内部状态中被压缩或坍缩，可供核查「以目标函数诱导的不变性造成视觉信息损失」这一类问题；但该工作本身是图像生成质量指标，与 latent 推理状态、生成与停止决策无直接联系。
